signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Tension + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.34, currently holding below its SMA20/50 cluster near 160.79-161.13. Head of Iran's paramilitary Basij has claimed the Strait of Hormuz is under Iran's control, introducing a significant geopolitical risk layer to the pair. Despite a 266bp OIS carry advantage for the USD, the options market is aggressively hedging for downside with the 1-month 25d risk reversal at -2.16, a strong put skew. Speculative positioning remains heavily net short JPY at -63,633 contracts, creating a high-conviction environment for a short squeeze if geopolitical escalation triggers a flight to safety. While VIX at 14.7 currently reflects low volatility, any spike above 25 would likely catalyze a rapid carry unwind toward the SMA200 at 158.15. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; geopolitical risk outweighs carry advantage. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 57% hike priced) 18 Sep — hike bias intact. Risk: Geopolitical tensions de-escalate and USD/JPY resumes its grind toward the 160.00 intervention watch level.

signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Commodity Divergence
signals.text: CAD/JPY represents the dominant G10 bilateral theme this week with a 1.263% performance spread. CAD leads the G10 with a +0.632% weekly average despite a -1.55% intraday drop in WTI oil, while JPY laggards at -0.631% across 7 pairs. This divergence is supported by a +125bp OIS carry advantage favoring the CAD over JPY. COT data shows CAD speculative positioning at a net short extreme of -102,309 (15.9% long), while JPY is also heavily short at -63,633. The CAD outperformance amid weak oil prices and crowded shorts suggests a structural repricing or short-covering flow is underway. USD/CAD technicals confirm the CAD bid, with the pair trading at 1.3952, well below its SMA20/50 cluster. Trade bias: Long CAD/JPY; bilateral G10 theme strength persists. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: WTI oil falls below $80, dragging CAD lower and compressing the G10 performance spread.

signals.title: GBP/USD — COT-OIS Alignment + Vol Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3485, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3369-1.3423). Speculative positioning is heavily net long at +39,039 (70.1% long), aligning with a restrictive real policy rate of +0.93%. The options market is pricing in significant protection with an 11.0% ATM IV against a 6.0% realized HV30, resulting in a notable +5.0% Vol Risk Premium. This elevated premium suggests institutional desks are paying up for tails rather than following a simple momentum trade. While the nominal Fed-BoE spread is neutral at 0bp, the GBP's 1W G10 outperformance (+0.372%) confirms the currency remains a preferred long. Continued gains are likely to test the 1.3500 handle if US data remains moderately negative (ESI -10.4). Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD; supported by real rates and positive technical posture. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) 17 Sep. Risk: UK GDP slowdown headlines intensify, causing a liquidation of the crowded +39k spec long.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning vs Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD at 0.7052 is holding above its SMA cluster, currently underpinned by a -71bp OIS carry premium against the USD. COT data reveals institutional bulls are in control with a +37,990 net long position (72.1% long). This contrasts sharply with retail sentiment, where 78% of traders are short, creating a classic institutional-vs-retail divergence. While the AUD Economic Surprise Index (ESI) is currently negative at -10.4, the technical position remains bullish as long as the pair holds above the SMA20 at 0.7016. Retail fading of the institutional trend often precedes further upside extension as retail shorts are forced to cover. Watch for a break of the recent high to confirm trend continuation. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; contrarian retail short bias supports the institutional long. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: Global risk-off sentiment shifts VIX above 20, favoring the USD's restrictive real rate of +1.52%.
